name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
description: Layer and annotate the ATT&CK matrix to map detection coverage against the techniques your sector actually faces.

name: CyberChef
description: The cyber swiss army knife — encode, decode, decompress, extract and transform data in the browser without touching a shell.

name: Elastic Security / Kibana
description: Open detection engineering stack with prebuilt rules, timeline investigation and endpoint telemetry in one place.

name: VirusTotal
description: Multi-engine file and URL scanning with behaviour graphs. Use the original hash, not the redirect, when enriching IOCs.

name: MISP / OpenCTI
description: Threat intelligence platforms for sharing, correlating and exporting indicators with your partners.

name: LOLBAS Project
description: Living off the Land Binaries and Scripts — the definitive catalogue of dual-use Windows binaries with usage examples.

name: GTFOBins
description: Unix equivalents: how common binaries can be abused for privilege escalation, shell escapes and file read/write.

name: LOLRuckets
description: Runtime packer catalog for binaries that are legitimately packed — reduces false positives in static analysis.

name: Wazuh
description: Open-source XDR/SIEM with file integrity monitoring, log collection and built-in detection rules.

name: Microsoft Sentinel
description: Cloud-native SIEM with KQL analytics, fusion correlation and a large community rule ecosystem.

name: Splunk Enterprise Security
description: Correlation search framework that made risk-based alerting mainstream — home of the SPL hunting tradition.

name: Sigma Rules Repository
description: Thousands of portable detection rules you can convert to your SIEM's language — start here before writing your own.

name: Wireshark
description: The packet analysis standard: dissect, filter and follow streams across hundreds of protocols.

name: Zeek
description: Network monitoring framework that turns traffic into structured logs (conn, dns, http, ssl) ideal for hunting.

name: NetworkMiner
description: Forensic PCAP viewer that extracts files, images and credentials straight out of capture files.

name: tcpdump / tshark CLI
description: Scriptable capture and filtering for responders who need answers without a GUI on the box.

name: OSCP — Offensive Security
description: Hands-on penetration testing certification. Still the most respected practical entry ticket for red teamers.

name: GCFA — GIAC Forensic Analyst
description: Digital forensics and incident response certification covering disk, memory and Windows artefact analysis.

name: GNFA — GIAC Network Forensic Analyst
description: Network-focused forensics: PCAP analysis, protocol reconstruction and lateral movement tracing.

name: BTL1 — Blue Team Level 1
description: Practical blue team foundation: SIEM, forensics, threat hunting and incident response in one lab-heavy course.

name: CRTO — Red Team Ops
description: Cobalt Strike and adversary emulation focused certification with a strong defensive-read audience too.

name: Project KillChain VAPT Format
description: The community reporting template this Hub's Report Builder implements — scope, findings, CVSS and remediation.

name: Pentester's Report Checklist
description: A short list of what turns a findings dump into something an engineering team will actually fix.

name: Shodan
description: Search engine for internet-exposed devices — see what the outside world sees before an attacker does.

name: Censys
description: Certificate and host intelligence for attack surface management and historical exposure tracking.

name: AbuseIPDB
description: Community-sourced IP reputation for fast triage of inbound sources. Correlate with your own logs before blocking.

name: Kali Linux
description: The best-known offensive security distribution — full toolchain for assessments and lab work.

name: REMnux
description: Linux distro for reverse engineering and malware analysis — tuned for detonating and inspecting samples safely.

name: Flare-VM
description: Windows toolkit distribution for reverse engineering: debuggers, disassemblers and analysis utilities preinstalled.

name: C2 Matrix
description: Comparison matrix of command-and-control frameworks — reference only, for detecting their default artefacts.

name: Atomic Red Team
description: Small, scripted attack simulations mapped to ATT&CK — the fastest way to test whether a detection works.

name: Caldera
description: MITRE's automated adversary emulation platform for repeatable purple team exercises.

name: Metasploit Unleashed Notes
description: Community courseware documenting exploitation concepts so defenders know exactly what artefacts to hunt.
